report.title: Driver arrested in Ceuta port as 300 kg hashish found in truck
report.summary: Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta after finding a hidden compartment packed with bags of hashish. Outlets estimate the haul at about 300 kilograms, pending an official weighing, and a court ordered the driver held in pre-trial prison on 15 November.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. On Sunday 15 November the judicial authority ordered the truck driver held in pre-trial prison for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments.

open_questions: Sources disagree on the exact date: Daily Thanthi describes the car stop as happening on Friday 6 November 2026, while Dinamani says the two women were arrested on Thursday night, 5 November.
No charges, court outcome or remand detail was reported; the case was at the investigation stage.

The Tamil outlets appear to reproduce the same Pudukkottai police account and are not independent reporting.
report.body:
Police in Pudukkottai stopped a car arriving from Andhra Pradesh and seized 26
kg of ganja. The packets were found stacked in a concealed compartment of
the car. Two women, Vasanthi and her sister's daughter Shanmugapriya, were
arrested at the scene. The ganja was valued at about 13 lakh rupees and the
car used for the smuggling was also seized.

Dinamalar named the women as Vasanthi, 55, and Shanmugapriya, 35. The
district police special division picked them up at Kattiyavayal and handed them
to the Pudukkottai Madurai enforcement division. Police registered a case
and a preliminary inquiry found the pair had planned to distribute the ganja to
local agents in Pudukkottai and surrounding areas. Officers said they were
investigating the interstate ganja smuggling network behind the consignment.

Dinamani reported that two women were arrested with 26 kg of ganja. Thanthi
TV reported that police arrested the two women who brought 26 kg of ganja by car
from Andhra Pradesh to Pudukkottai.

report.title: Two arrested in Thiaroye Kao with 44 pieces of kush
report.summary: Police in Yeumbeul Sud arrested two men in Thiaroye Kao, a Dakar suburb, and seized 44 pieces of kush, 3,000 CFA francs and a mobile phone. The two admitted owning the drugs but refused to name their supplier, and an investigation was opened.
report.body:
Police in the Dakar suburb of Thiaroye Kao arrested two men on 13 November 2026
in an operation by the research brigade of the Yeumbeul Sud police station.
The operation followed an anonymous tip about intense kush trafficking, and
plainclothes officers raided the reported places around 8 a.m. Kush is
cannabis.

The first suspect, identified as P. Ngom, was caught packaging narcotics near
the Thiaroye Market. Officers found 20 pieces of kush hidden in a
broken-down vehicle tyre. They also found 3,000 CFA francs and an Infinix
mobile phone in his possession. The second suspect, E. L. Welle, was
arrested near the footbridge at the Thiaroye TER station with 24 pieces of kush
concealed under his clothing.

In all, police seized 44 pieces of kush, 3,000 CFA francs and a mobile phone,
all placed under seal. The two men admitted owning the seized narcotics but
refused to reveal their supplier's identity. The prosecutor was informed
and an investigation opened to establish the extent of the alleged activity and
identify the supplier. A second report confirmed the seizure of 44 pieces
of kush, 3,000 CFA francs and a mobile phone.

attempts.decision_title: DUI checkpoint arrests are not a cannabis event
attempts.explanation: The opened article reports a Concord, California DUI checkpoint held on 13 November 2026 at Clayton Road and Ayers Road, during which officers contacted 616 vehicles and arrested two people for driving under the influence. No cannabis was seized, and no cannabis possession, sale, cultivation or trafficking charge is reported; the two arrests were for DUI. Marijuana is mentioned only to remind readers that driving under its influence remains illegal, and the checkpoint's funding came from a Cannabis Tax Fund Grant. A traffic-safety grant and a warning about impaired driving do not make this a cannabis enforcement event, so it falls outside the tracker's substance scope. No existing report matches it.
